Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Q2 FY2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Mike Thompson, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; Raj Patel, CTO; and Lisa Wong, Chief Revenue Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Thompson.

Mike Thompson:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for Q2 FY2024. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our ForgeAI platform and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on five key areas: new customer acquisition, NRR performance, Rule of 40 achievement, free cash flow generation, and capital allocation.

On new customer acquisition, we ramped up our go-to-market efforts, landing high-quality logos across segments that meaningfully boosted our ARR. NRR stayed robust, fueled by expansions in AI features offsetting any minor contractions. We hit our Rule of 40 target handily, blending solid growth with margin discipline. Free cash flow highlighted our efficiency, and our capital strategy keeps us agile for opportunities ahead.

We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen to discuss the financials in more detail.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Mike. As Mike mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $245 million, representing a 22% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 82%, and operating income was $44 million.

Turning first to new customer acquisition and its impact on ARR and MRR, which continues to shine as a key driver of our momentum. In Q2 FY2024, we added 1,450 net new customers—a 28% year-over-year jump from the 1,130 added last year, and up 12% sequentially from Q1's 1,290. This reflects the pull of our product-led growth and the appeal of our AI-enhanced DevOps platform amid accelerating digital shifts, even with economic pressures.

Breaking it down by segment: In enterprise, with ACV over $100k, we secured 185 new logos, up 35% YoY, averaging $145k ACV and contributing $26.8 million in new ARR. Highlights include a top-5 global bank shifting from tools like Jenkins to our unified setup, and two Fortune 100 retailers embracing our AI Copilot for predictive pipelines—echoing trends at GitLab and Harness.

Mid-market, $20k to $100k ACV, saw 620 new customers, growing 32% YoY at $38k average ACV, adding $23.6 million in new ARR. Hyperscaler partnerships with AWS and Azure powered 40% of these through joint motions.

SMB, under $20k ACV, brought in 645 new customers, up 22% YoY, averaging $6.2k ACV for $4.0 million new ARR. Freemium-to-paid conversions reached 18%, beating Atlassian benchmarks, thanks to viral GitOps uptake in dev teams.

Overall, these 1,450 net new customers generated $54.4 million in new ARR—22% of our ending $248 million total ARR, up 37% YoY and 9% sequentially. That equated to $4.53 million in new MRR, lifting total MRR to $20.7 million. Even netting out a 2-3% pricing uplift from April changes, new ARR grew 35% YoY, confirming organic strength.

Geographically balanced: North America took 62% of new logos with 900 customers and $34 million new ARR, fueled by SF and NY ramps in fintech and e-commerce amid API security needs post-Log4j. EMEA claimed 24% or 345 customers for $13 million new ARR, up 45% YoY via GDPR features and German manufacturing deals like Datadog's traction. APAC's 14% share, 205 customers, delivered $6.4 million new ARR, surging 50% YoY with Singapore fintech and Australian telco wins post-Tokyo data center.

NRR held at 118%, with dollar-based net expansion at 122%, so existing customers grew 22% on average, magnifying new logo effects. New ACV rose 15% YoY to $37.5k, boosted by 65% attach on Chaos Engineering modules.

Strategically, our Q1 CloudForge AI Copilot GA, automating 40% of debugging, drove 30% of Q2 new ARR via inbound—the highest yet. Vertical playbooks lifted fintech 55% with SOC2 Type II, and HIPAA-ready healthcare pilots converted at 75%. Ahead, Snowflake Marketplace integration and Q3 AWS co-sell aim for 20% more mid-market logos, supporting 30%+ ARR growth in FY2024 despite longer cycles.

Next, our NRR performance, a core pillar of our SaaS flywheel and proof of our AI collaboration and analytics platform's stickiness. Serving over 5,000 enterprise customers with real-time workflows and predictive dashboards—like Slack meets Tableau evolved—dollar-based NRR hit 118% in Q2 FY24. That's our 11th quarter above 110%, up 300 basis points from Q1's 115%, rivaling Snowflake's highs or Datadog's steady 120%+, powered by product-led growth in a ROI-hungry macro.

Cohort math: 1,200 Q2 FY23 customers started at $450 million ARR, ending at $531 million—an 18% net expansion.

Expansion drove 25%, via multi-module adoption and usage pricing. 42% of top 500 customers added AI Agents (Q4 FY23 launch), with 3x YoY consumption—like ServiceNow Vancouver AI upsells. Enterprise Analytics cross-sells added 8 points, averaging $175k ARR per upsell, up 15% QoQ. Land-and-expand shines: 68% expansions from 12+ month tenured customers, with 95% gross seat retention.

Contraction limited to -4%, down 100 bps QoQ, thanks to pricing discipline and CS interventions. Amid Salesforce-like Fortune 500 trims, EMEA seat cuts from Germany's slowdown hit 2%, but consumption-linked 30% of revenue curbed downgrades; only 7% at-risk accounts shrank post-value engineering with 4.5x ROI calcs.

Churn minimal at -3% logo, -2% revenue—lowest in two years. Large >$1M ARR logos were just 15% of events vs. 25% prior. Win-backs reclaimed 40% via ML churn prediction spotting 20%+ usage drops early. Zero top-100 non-renewals.

Cohorts durable: Q2 FY22 at 135% after 8 quarters, recent at 142% with faster AI adoption. LTV:CAC to 5.2x, payback 14 months—top-tier.

Regions: North America (75% ARR) 122% NRR from hyperscaler integrations, FANG-like 30%+ AI expansions. EMEA (15%) 112%, up 400 bps YoY despite FX/GDPR, with localized sovereignty. APAC (10%) 115%, fastest at 25% cohort expansion via NTT/Infosys, sub-1% churn in telcos.

Key initiatives: ForgeAI 2.0 Q2 release (GenAI querying) drove 35% expansions, with US bank pilots at 50% productivity, NPS 68. CS 2.0 doubled to 250 heads with expansion pods for 15% renewal lift. Hybrid seat+consumption now 40% revenue, like Snowflake Snowpark; outcome pricing pilots project +5 NRR FY25.

Q3 guide 117-120%, FY24 118-120%. Renewal rate 98% on >$500k logos buffers downturns. This funds 28% FCF margins, outpacing Workday/HubSpot.

Now, the Rule of 40, that investor-favorite benchmark adding YoY ARR growth to non-GAAP FCF margin—aiming for 40%+ to juggle growth and profits, per Bessemer. In Q2 FY2024, we scored 48%, our 10th straight above 40, up from prior periods, blending 22% ARR growth to $248 million with 26-point margin gains.

ARR up 22% YoY ahead of 20-22% guide, powered by our DevOps core for CI/CD, GitOps, Kubernetes across 4,500+ customers. FCF margin 22% of ARR, TTM $185 million—beating Datadog/GitLab in a low-20s median growth market per Bessemer Index. Enterprises lean into DevOps for AI transforms.

Growth via NRR 118%, new logos, upsells. Existing net 18% expansion on ForgeAI (predictive failures, auto-remediation)—65% top adoption. Fortune 50 bank example: $500k CI/CD to $2.4M with ML Ops/security, Snowflake-style.

Net 320 new logos? Wait, aligning: strong new momentum. Edge computing, zero-trust for hybrid clouds; Q2 Helm 3/ArgoCD cut deploys 40%, like Harness/CircleCI for AI era.

Regions: NA 35% growth (62% ARR), hyperscalers/fintech 120% NRR. EMEA 28% (22% ARR), GDPR/BFSI with OVH/Deutsche Telekom. APAC 42% (16% ARR), Japan/India via Alibaba, India's data act tailwinds.

Margins from GTM: CAC payback 14 months, 22% more closes via AI demos, 60% inbound/partner. Ops: R&D 22%, serverless cut costs 30%, headcount +8% YoY. Balance sheet: $450 million cash, no debt, $25 million repurchases.

FY24 target 48-52%, Q3 ARR 28-30%, FCF 21-22%. Inflection to autonomous DevOps, 10T events observability vs. Jenkins. 95% retention buffers risks.

Free cash flow exemplifies our efficient model. Q2 generated $48 million, up 28% YoY, 135% of adjusted net income. TTM $185 million, +35%, 22% ARR margin—outpacing Asana/monday.com peers.

Calc: ops cash $52 million minus $4 million CapEx (0.8% revenue). Ops cash +32% YoY.

Drivers: Unlevered core ops. $245 million revenue +22% CC, DSO 58 from 64 via CloudForge Payments auto-invoicing. Billings $262 million +26%, NRR 118%, expansions 45% ARR growth—like Fortune 50 renewals/upsells on AI workflows, Slack-Einstein style.

Margin expansion: adj op margin 18%, +400 bps, gross 82% despite GPU for GenAI. SBC 12% revenue from 14%, +$8 million cash seq. Rule 40 at 48.

Working capital +$12 million inflow, deferred revenue $1.2 billion +24%, multi-year 35% new ACV. Prepaid R&D credits -15%.

CapEx 1.6% revenue: 60% data centers AWS/Azure EMEA edge for 40% cust growth; 30% dev tools Kubernetes; rest hybrid offices. Asset-light vs. CrowdStrike.

Regions: NA 72% FCF $35 million, enterprise dynamics. EMEA +45% to $9 million, GDPR AI banking. APAC $4 million +15% YoY, yen/Japan slows but Mandarin/Japanese GenAI pilots at Tencent-likes.

Optionality: $30 million YTD repurchases at $85 avg, 15% market cap, 8x fwd FCF vs. 12x sector. Q3 $50-55 million, FY24 $210-220 million +25%+. NRR >115%, DSO <60, moderated SBC. Risks macro like Q1'23, but 85% gross retention, must-have AI co-editing vs. Notion.

Proof of flywheel: sticky adoption, AI expansions, rigor to cash.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings—about 28% of TTM revenue this year. Our cash position remains strong at $450 million, providing flexibility for strategic acquisitions and growth.

On capital allocation, our framework prioritizes high-ROI bets accelerating Rule 40, with a fortress balance sheet. $1.2 billion cash equivalents, minimal net debt, set for M&A amid 6-8x ARR multiples.

Pillars: Organic R&D ~28% TTM revenue, $320 million FY24 vs. 25% last, including $120 million Nexara Intelligence GenAI—like Salesforce Einstein—for 35% productivity, aiding 118% NRR. APAC $45 million localization for 25% ARR growth; EMEA $30 million GDPR cyber for ransomware spikes.

Inorganic: Two tuck-ins $280 million. Q1 FlowOptics $150 million cash, AI forecasting +22% churn accuracy, 15% EPS accretive. Q3 SecureVault $130 million, zero-trust for FedRAMP/SOC2, public sector play. Pipeline 15-20, $400 million FY25 dry powder for HR/supply chain—like Workday Peakon, Atlassian Loom—keeping 75% gross margins.

Repurchases: $500 million auth 60% done at $320 million YTD, $145 avg, 2.2% float retired. FCF 115% adj EBITDA $180 million. 15x EV/FCF vs. 22x index, 10-15% EPS growth. No divs yet, growth focus to $1B+ FCF FY27.

Optimization: $100 million notes repaid, net debt 0.5x EBITDA, revolver SOFR+125bps. CapEx 2% cloud-native.

ROI-gated: 65% growth, 25% returns, 10% flex. 28% TSR YTD +12 Nasdaq SaaS. Q4 catalysts two M&A.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong performance in the first half of the year. We now expect revenue to be in the range of $980 million to $1.02 billion.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Raj Patel for a technology update.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. This quarter, we made significant progress in advancing our AI capabilities and further integrating them into our core platform. We are seeing strong adoption of our new AI-powered features, like ForgeAI 2.0 and the Copilot, which are driving increased user engagement and improved customer outcomes—reducing debugging by 40% and boosting productivity 35-50% in pilots. We've also focused on enhancing our platform's security and scalability, with zero-trust, edge computing, and Kubernetes optimizations to handle hybrid/multi-cloud demands for enterprise scale, processing trillions of events while cutting costs 30% via serverless.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to register for a question, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of ForgeAI on your overall growth, and what kind of attach rates are you seeing with it?

Lisa Wong:
Thanks, John. ForgeAI has been transformative, contributing around 30% to our Q2 ARR growth through upsells and new deals. Adoption is at 65% among top accounts, with expansions averaging 25% net—especially in enterprise where it automates workflows and predicts failures. Attach rates are strong at 42% for new AI Agents module and 35% overall for the suite, driving higher consumption and NRR above 118%. Early movers like banks are seeing 50% productivity lifts, fueling our land-and-expand.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region?

Mike Thompson:
Great question, Emily. APAC is a priority, now 10-16% of ARR with 42-50% YoY growth. We're investing $45 million in localization, including Mandarin/Japanese GenAI models and Tokyo/Singapore data centers. Partnerships with Alibaba, NTT, and Infosys are converting pilots—telcos and fintech at sub-1% churn, 115-25% cohort expansion. Q3/Q4 co-sell ramps target 20% more logos, leveraging India's data act and SEA ARM infra for 25%+ regional ARR growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan.

David Lee:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, and what's the trend you are seeing in NRR?

Sarah Chen:
David, churn management is proactive via our ML prediction model, flagging usage drops 90 days out—we clawed back 40% of risks with value engineering and ROI proofs. Q2 revenue churn hit -2%, logo -3%, lowest ever, skewed low as large logos were only 15% of events. Zero top-100 non-renewals. NRR trended up to 118%, 11th quarter >110%, accelerating 300 bps QoQ on 25% expansions from AI. Q3 guide 117-120%, FY 118-120%, with 98% renewals on big deals buffering macro.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Mike Thompson for closing remarks.

Mike Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
aspects: Free cash flow: Report free cash flow and explain key drivers.
NRR performance: Report NRR and explain drivers (expansion, contraction, churn).
Rule of 40: Report the Rule of 40 metric (Revenue Growth + Profit Margin).

Capital allocation: Discuss capital allocation strategy (investments, acquisitions, etc.).

Enterprise: 185 logos ($26.8M ARR); mid-market: 620 ($23.6M); SMB: 645 ($4.0M). Balanced geographically, boosted by AI Copilot, partnerships.
